newsitem.title: USA: GTE probed by Calif. regulators - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: GTE probed by Calif. regulators - WSJ.

text.p: California regulators are investigating GTE Corp for allegedly destroying or withholding documents involved in a false-billing probe, the Wall Street Journal said.
In Thursday's electronic edition, the Journal said GTE also has hired former California Supreme Court Chief Justice Malcolm Lucas to head an internal inquiry into the matter.

Wilson Lewis, who heads utility enforcement for the California Public Utilities Commission, told the Journal that the allegations are "serious," and, if true, "there's a word for it -- it's called obstruction of justice."
The allegations are part of an ongoing race-bias and whistle-blower lawsuit involving allegations it charged Spanish-speaking customers for services that had not been ordered.
GTE contends that employees at its Language Assistance Center billed those customers without the knowledge or consent of the company.
GTE said in a statement that it is cooperating with the investigation and that it "takes these allegations very seriously and is investigating them with the utmost urgency."
